activity.message:
Lay routes onto shared centre lines and show which way each stop serves

- Routes on the same street now follow one shared centre line, so their lanes are parallel; lane changes slide in small steps, or happen at once near a turn; bus bays no longer bulge. A saved older drawing is shown until the new one is ready, and the drawing is only computed when the timetable or the method changes.
- Stops say which way their buses go (from the feed's cardinal_direction): in the stop sheet, search, planner steps, share text and timetable, and with an arrow on the map. A stop served both ways labels each departure.
- feedanalysis overview exports the layout to GeoJSON for checking it in a browser.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Merge route directions into one line with smooth lanes, and fix the menu over the journey

- The network view draws one line per route (directions and variants merged where they share streets) and lays routes that share a street side by side, with lanes decided by the neighbouring routes, smoothed over about 100 m, kept for at least about 160 m and ramped between; spikes out to a stop are removed. A route on its own still shows each direction on the street.
- Opening the menu puts any sheet away; the journey sheet can be dragged down into the bar, and the bar swiped up again. A swipe from the left edge opens the menu.
- The collector stores snapshots as sent (gzip cost more CPU than the free plan allows), keeps 6 days, and the pull skips what the Mac recorder already saved. MIT licence. The 24-hour feed report.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Make routes easier to read and plan trips with stops on the way

- Routes that share a street are drawn side by side in lanes instead of on top of each other; both directions of a route share a lane, and a route crossing a street is not pushed sideways.
- Tapping lines of several routes asks which one; tapping one route no longer moves the camera, and tapping the empty map lets go of it.
- The route list and the focus chip say how many buses run in each direction, or why there are none (not running today, between trips, not reporting), with the next trip.
- Faded routes can be made fainter (default much fainter); the alert chip explains the dashed line.
- A trip can have up to three stops on the way, each with a stay time, also working backwards from an arrival time; saved trips sit under the saved places and keep their stops, and more recent trips are shown.
